A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RA-Det work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison. The original appendices are retained as Appendices C and D in v2, alongside new material.

before.justification: V1 reports original cross-generator detection results, component ablations, JPEG/blur robustness experiments, and DDPM feature-shift experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds training-source comparisons, recent-generator evaluations, further ablations, efficiency measurements, and AMS-based memorization analysis.

M1.justification: The frozen encoder, conditional-UNet probing module, semantic/discrepancy/residual branches, fusion, and composite loss remain unchanged. Alternative probes and contrastive margins are experimental controls, not revisions to the proposed detector.

E1.justification: Table 4 adds seven generator columns: SDXL, SDv3.5, FLUX, FLUX1-dev, MJ-v6, Infinity, and VAR. This extends evaluation to newer synthesis systems and autoregressive generation. Appendix A also introduces diffusion-source and mixed-source training using SDv1.4 data from AIGIBench/GenImage. The original benchmark and CelebA-HQ study remain.

E2.justification: C2P-CLIP, previously discussed only in related work, becomes an evaluated efficiency comparator alongside UniFD in v2 Table 5. The detector membership in Table 1 and the JPEG/blur comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds SDv1.4-only training with 52,922 real/72,000 fake images and mixed-source training with 72,000/72,000, alongside the retained ProGAN 360,000/360,000 setting. It introduces fixed-probe controls, a five-value margin sweep, AMS-based evaluation, and matched-hardware efficiency measurements. Appendix D.2 also changes the stated epoch-analysis aggregation from epsilon values generally to small-epsilon values; the PDFs do not establish that the retained plots were recomputed.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained backbone, loss, branch, and post-processing analyses, v2 tests learned probing against Gaussian noise, Gaussian blur, and resize residuals; examines margin sensitivity and training-source dependence; and analyzes computational cost. Appendix D.2 adds AMS-based validation of the memorization relationship, addressing a question previously investigated only through training epochs.

E5.justification: V1 Figure 6 already reports linear fits with slopes and R-squared values. V2 applies this estimation approach to AMS in Table 6, adding point-estimate results rather than a new uncertainty-reporting practice. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the retained ablation scores are unchanged, including RA-Det's 93.47% ACC/97.00% AP. V2 adds substantial results: for example, ProGAN-trained RA-Det scores 57.19%/61.50% on FLUX in Table 4, fixed-probe variants achieve 86.11–87.07% ACC in Table 3, and AMS regressions have positive slopes with R-squared values of 0.59–0.73. Efficiency results are new, and Figure 2 replaces the CLIP similarity distribution.

T1.justification: V2 removes Appendix B.2's explicit inequality asserting that SIDE divergence strictly decreases with training epochs and withdraws its claimed theoretical justification. The central definitions, Assumption 4.1, Lemma 4.2, Theorem 4.3, and their proofs remain unchanged in Section 4 and the relocated Appendix D.1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about universal robustness asymmetry, its memorization connection, RA-Det, and detection superiority. The abstract's 7.81% improvement claim is unchanged; additional experiments support existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: Appendix D.2 reclassifies epoch-based evidence as a training-stage trend rather than a validated monotonic memorization proxy and interprets the new AMS associations as more direct support. V2 also discusses training-source independence, learned-probe necessity, inference overhead, and the limitations of single-generator training for real-world distributions. However, a retained paragraph and Figure 6's caption still describe epochs as a memorization proxy.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly identifies LSUN and AIGIBench/GenImage provenance and gives training-source sample counts. The stated hardware changes from four NVIDIA 4090 GPUs to eight H200 GPUs, and Table 5 reports compute, parameters, memory, and latency. Core training hyperparameters and the code link remain unchanged; the hardware revision alone does not establish reruns.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for new generators and data sources, including Infinity, VAR, SDXL, FLUX, LSUN, AIGIBench, and GenImage. The appearance-versus-behavior positioning remains intact. Publication updates to existing references and consolidation of the duplicated Hounie citation do not represent newly introduced works.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and most introductory, methodological, theoretical, and concluding text remain intact. V2 locally rewrites ablation, robustness, and epoch-validation discussions; adds generality and efficiency subsections, acknowledgements, and an impact statement; updates the publication header; and reorganizes the appendices around the additions.

P2.justification: V2 adds four tables covering training-source summaries, detailed generator results, efficiency, and AMS regression, and expands/regroups the original ablation table. Figure 2 replaces the CLIP histogram and fixes panel labels; Figure 4 gains a detailed caption. Figures 5 and 6 are relocated, with their original plotted results retained.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central mechanism: v1 lacked fixed-probe controls and relied on an asserted epoch-to-memorization relationship; v2 adds probing controls and AMS-based evidence. Training-source and contemporary-generator tests, together with measured computational costs, also improve assessment of applicability. These address important evidential gaps. The gains are tempered by Table 4's unclear averaging scope and the contradictory epoch-proxy wording retained in Figure 6.
